speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had fatigue, flank pain, and fever following antibiotic treatment for sinusitis. When did these symptoms start, and have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as frequency, urgency, or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: That suggests the infection may have spread to your kidneys. Have you noticed any blood in your urine, or have you experienced nausea and vomiting alongside the fever? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and CBC.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophilic casts and granular cells in your urinalysis strongly suggests acute interstitial nephritis rather than a typical bacterial kidney infection, especially given your recent antibiotic use. Did you experience a rash, hives, or joint pain along with these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to amoxicillin/cephalexin hypersensitivity. The timeline of rash onset, antibiotic use, and subsequent development of fever, flank pain, and eosinophilic urinary findings confirms this allergic reaction to the kidneys.
